# A `payment:` block whose `amount:` is finer than the account holding it.
#
# 18.19 is a fine number of Canadian dollars and not a whole number of the
# units this receivable is kept in — its Smallest Fraction is a dollar. The
# settling split lands on that account and is stored at its unit, so the
# amount came out 18 against a value of 18.19 on a same-currency split, and
# the export wrote `amount: 18` back.
#
# The payment path judged the figure against the currency alone, so the
# account arm of the check — which exists for exactly this — never ran here.
#
# What this fixture produces: a refusal naming 18.19 and the account's whole
# dollar, and no payment.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_amount_must_fit_the_currency.py.
2026-01-01 open Assets
	type: Asset
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Accounts Receivable
	type: Accounts Receivable
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
	commodity_scu: 1
2026-01-01 open Income
	type: Income
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Income:Sales
	type: Income
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"

customer "C-COARSE"
	name: "Coarse Customer"
	currency: CAD

invoice "INV-COARSE-001"
	customer_id: "C-COARSE"
	currency: CAD
	date_opened: 2026-01-05
	entry:
		date: 2026-01-05
		description: "Consulting"
		action: "Hours"
		account: "Income:Sales"
		quantity: 1
		price: 100
		taxable: false
		tax_included: false
	posted:
		date: 2026-01-05
		due: 2026-02-05
		ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable"
		memo: "Invoice INV-COARSE-001"
		accumulate: true
	payment:
		date: 2026-02-25
		amount: 18.19
		account: "Assets:Bank"
		memo: "Payment for INV-COARSE-001"
